messages:
sam: Heads-up — I pushed a small TF change to swap the model-service env ConfigMap to use `envFrom: secretRef` for db creds. Need a quick review, planning a hotpatch apply in ~15m if no objections.

sam: Reason: leak of a test key in the configmap during last deploy. We should avoid plaintext. This is small and isolated to model-service namespace.

maria: Can you paste the `kubectl` diff / the TF plan output? Want to verify there are no pod restarts that could drop inference traffic. :eyes:

sam: Plan snippet:```diff
@@ resource "kubernetes_config_map" "model_service_env" {
  data = {
-    DB_URL = "postgres://...:5432/models"
+    # removed DB_URL, replaced by secret reference
  }
}
@@
+resource "kubernetes_secret" "model_service_db" {
+  metadata { name = "model-service-db-creds" }
+  data = { DB_URL = base64encode(var.db_url) }
+}
```
No change to deployment manifest; pods reference `envFrom` already but pointed at a non-prod secret before, now it's wired to the new secret. TF plan shows no `kubectl rollout restart` directives.

josh: If pods already reference the secret via `envFrom`, swapping the configmap -> secret shouldn't cause restarts unless the Deployment spec content changes. But double-check if we're also changing an annotation that triggers rolling update.

sam: Confirmed — only resource changes are the configmap removal + secret addition. Deployment `spec.template` untouched. TF state will `delete` the configmap and `create` secret. K8s won't restart pods on secret change (envFrom doesn't auto-reload), so pods continue running with old env until they recreate. That means current pods keep old value until a restart / rollout.

kate: That's important — we might want to force a rollout after apply to ensure no pods keep the leaked value. Suggest a canary: restart 1 replica first, validate, then rest. Ops window?

sam: Yup plan was: apply -> rollout restart for 1 pod -> health check -> rollout rest. Commands I would run after successful apply:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-service -n model-service --selector=app=model-service --timeout=2m
# or to restart a single pod
kubectl delete pod $(kubectl get pods -n model-service -l app=model-service -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -n model-service
```

maria: Quick question about rollback: if apply fails or we see issues, what's easiest? Recreate the configmap from backup and reapply? TF will try to delete then recreate on rollback — can we just restore configmap with `kubectl apply -f`?

josh: Yes — easiest emergency rollback is to reapply the previous configmap YAML (we have it in the infra repo under `env-backups/`). Do that, then if necessary run `terraform state rm kubernetes_config_map.model_service_env` to remove the dangling TF resource and avoid immediate re-deletion on next plan. Then we can import it back if we want TF to manage it again.

sam: Noted. I'll keep `env-backups/model-service-configmap.yaml` handy. Also tagging the apply with a comment: `hotpatch/env-swap/1843216780`.

deploy-bot: terraform plan complete — 1 to add, 1 to destroy. (reacted :rocket:)

kate: When you run apply, please post the `terraform apply -auto-approve` output and I'll run the canary pod restart + smoke checks. If any 5xx errors spike, I'll revert manually.

sam: Will do. ETA 13m. If anyone wants to pair during the apply ping me @maria @josh.

josh: Also check RBAC: secrets must be in same ns and accessible by the SA used by pods. If TF created secret in another ns by mistake, pods won't see it.

sam: Good call — secret is created in `model-service` ns. Verified in plan.

kate: Awesome. Thx. If no objections, give :thumbsup: here and proceed.

maria: +1 :thumbsup:

josh: +1

sam: Started `terraform apply` now. Pasting output shortly.

deploy-bot: terraform apply complete — applied 1 add, 1 delete. state id: abc123.

sam: Apply succeeded. Doing single-pod restart now.

deploy-bot: pod/model-service-2 restarted — ready.

kate: Running smoke tests on canary... all good (latency within baseline, no 5xx). Proceeding to roll rest.

sam: Rolling remaining pods.

deploy-bot: rollout complete — 3/3 updated.

maria: Verified no leaked keys in current pods' env. Good job. Please file a short postmortem note in the infra repo about the leak cause and add a gating check to catch plaintext creds in configmaps.

sam: Will open a short PR with a pre-apply grep and a brief incident note. Thanks everyone for quick eyes. :coffee:
